# How Clemson University's Peach Team is like the Avengers

DJ

Danielle Johnson

Share[Email](mailto:?subject=How%20Clemson%20University's%20Peach%20Team%20is%20like%20the%20Avengers&body=https%3A%2F%2F6amcity.com%2Fsc%2Fgreenville%2Fcity%2Fclemson-peach-team "Share via Email")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2F6amcity.com%2Fsc%2Fgreenville%2Fcity%2Fclemson-peach-team "Share on Facebook")[X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2F6amcity.com%2Fsc%2Fgreenville%2Fcity%2Fclemson-peach-team&text=How%20Clemson%20University%27s%20Peach%20Team%20is%20like%20the%20Avengers "Share on X")[Nextdoor](https://nextdoor.com/sharekit/?body=https%3A%2F%2F6amcity.com%2Fsc%2Fgreenville%2Fcity%2Fclemson-peach-team "Share on Nextdoor")

![Image 4: How Clemson University's Peach Team is like the Avengers](https://6amcity.com/web/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fbucketeer-d57e4b8a-9958-49c4-a7a0-a1659858cb32.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot-migration%2Fb2%2Ff3%2F6c4e396144dcb567f9656aeee3a2%2Fnewsletter-template-598-x-319-px-your-story-598-x-319-px-3.png&w=3840&q=75)

The goal: Perfect peaches. | Photo by GVLtoday

It's the orchard's last line of defense — a peninsula lab on Lake Hartwell where a team of scientists is [battling disease](https://www.foxcarolina.com/2022/09/16/researchers-working-combat-disease-impacting-sc-peaches/), drought, and time itself.

The peach industry relies on work happening at a strategically placed farm situated on a Lake Hartwell peninsula. They’re known as [Clemson's Peach Team](https://www.clemson.edu/extension/peach/team.html) — the largest group of scientists focused on peaches in the entire world — but after spending some time with them at the Musser Fruit Research Center, we caught a vibe that they’re the Avengers of the Peach Universe.

“We’re all internationals, recruited from other countries to work here, so you can claim they’ve got the best of the best,” said Dr. Guido Schnabel, Professor of Plant Pathology, when presented with our parallel. “We’re from all over the world, working here together for one thing: how to support the peach industry.”

We saw the orchards and inside the labs where this work is taking place, and here’s which Avenger each of these Protectors of the Peach reminded us of:

### **Dr. Guido Schnabel | Thor**

_Professor of Plant Pathology — Fruit Crops_  
“There are several diseases affecting the peach tree, and other diseases that might affect the fruit. I am working to try and find solutions to make sure our trees are surviving and our fruit is of high quality.” 
Like Thor, Dr. Schnabel is the _mighty guardian_ standing between the orchard and its greatest enemies — bacteria and fungi. For 25+ years, he’s wielded powerful tools from his resistance research just like Thor swings Mjolnir, striking down threats that would destroy entire harvests. He’s Clemson’s _protector of the orchard realm._

![Image 5](https://bucketeer-d57e4b8a-9958-49c4-a7a0-a1659858cb32.s3.amazonaws.com/public/brightspot-inline/b2/f3/6c4e396144dcb567f9656aeee3a2/newsletter-template-598-x-319-px-your-story-598-x-319-px-3.png)

The goal: Perfect peaches. | Photo by GVLtoday

### **Dr. Ksenija Gasic | Iron Man**

_Professor of Horticulture — Peach Genetics and Breeding_
“What can I give growers in 15 or 20 years? You cannot ask me now for something you want tomorrow. Sometimes I do things that they don’t want yet, but then suddenly, it becomes a thing.”

Just like Tony Stark builds new suits to solve impossible problems, Dr. Gasic designs better peach varieties using cutting-edge genomic tools. She’s not just fighting today’s pests — she’s future-proofing orchards for the next generation, like Stark building defenses for threats Earth (or in this case, growers) hasn’t seen yet.

### **Dr. Juan Carlos Melgar | Captain America**

_Associate Professor of Pomology_  
“I work on optimizing fertilization, irrigation, and soil health, which is reducing costs for growers. It’s sustainability, not only environmental sustainability, but it’s economic sustainability and sustaining the industry in the long term.” 
Like Cap, Dr. Melgar is on the front lines, working directly with growers to defend crops against harsh environments, pests, and stresses. Studying climates, balancing soil, water, and stress factors — he’s constantly adapting, like Captain America adjusting to every battlefield.

![Image 6](https://bucketeer-d57e4b8a-9958-49c4-a7a0-a1659858cb32.s3.amazonaws.com/public/brightspot-inline/f8/a4/849f6cfc468c89d2e8f4ea2f1b3f/newsletter-template-598-x-319-px-your-story-598-x-319-px-4.png)

"Earth's Mightiest Heroes" type thing. | Photo by GVLtoday

### **Jeff Hopkins | Nick Fury**

_Farm manager_  
“You don’t have research if you don’t have peaches.”
He sees the big picture and connects all the moving parts — like Fury bringing together the Avengers, he brings together the equipment, the experiments, and the day-to-day operations that keep the whole Peach Team running.

While we only met these four, much like the Marvel Cinematic Universe, [the whole team](https://www.clemson.edu/extension/peach/team.html) brings even more superpowers to the table, saving the peaches one tree at a time.

# How Clemson University's Peach Team is like the Avengers

DJ

Danielle Johnson

Share[Email](mailto:?subject=How%20Clemson%20University's%20Peach%20Team%20is%20like%20the%20Avengers&body=https%3A%2F%2F6amcity.com%2Fsc%2Fgreenville%2Fcity%2Fclemson-peach-team "Share via Email")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2F6amcity.com%2Fsc%2Fgreenville%2Fcity%2Fclemson-peach-team "Share on Facebook")[X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2F6amcity.com%2Fsc%2Fgreenville%2Fcity%2Fclemson-peach-team&text=How%20Clemson%20University%27s%20Peach%20Team%20is%20like%20the%20Avengers "Share on X")[Nextdoor](https://nextdoor.com/sharekit/?body=https%3A%2F%2F6amcity.com%2Fsc%2Fgreenville%2Fcity%2Fclemson-peach-team "Share on Nextdoor")

![Image 4: How Clemson University's Peach Team is like the Avengers](https://6amcity.com/web/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fbucketeer-d57e4b8a-9958-49c4-a7a0-a1659858cb32.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot-migration%2Fb2%2Ff3%2F6c4e396144dcb567f9656aeee3a2%2Fnewsletter-template-598-x-319-px-your-story-598-x-319-px-3.png&w=3840&q=75)

The goal: Perfect peaches. | Photo by GVLtoday

It's the orchard's last line of defense — a peninsula lab on Lake Hartwell where a team of scientists is [battling disease](https://www.foxcarolina.com/2022/09/16/researchers-working-combat-disease-impacting-sc-peaches/), drought, and time itself.

The peach industry relies on work happening at a strategically placed farm situated on a Lake Hartwell peninsula. They’re known as [Clemson's Peach Team](https://www.clemson.edu/extension/peach/team.html) — the largest group of scientists focused on peaches in the entire world — but after spending some time with them at the Musser Fruit Research Center, we caught a vibe that they’re the Avengers of the Peach Universe.

“We’re all internationals, recruited from other countries to work here, so you can claim they’ve got the best of the best,” said Dr. Guido Schnabel, Professor of Plant Pathology, when presented with our parallel. “We’re from all over the world, working here together for one thing: how to support the peach industry.”

We saw the orchards and inside the labs where this work is taking place, and here’s which Avenger each of these Protectors of the Peach reminded us of:

### **Dr. Guido Schnabel | Thor**

_Professor of Plant Pathology — Fruit Crops_  
“There are several diseases affecting the peach tree, and other diseases that might affect the fruit. I am working to try and find solutions to make sure our trees are surviving and our fruit is of high quality.” 
Like Thor, Dr. Schnabel is the _mighty guardian_ standing between the orchard and its greatest enemies — bacteria and fungi. For 25+ years, he’s wielded powerful tools from his resistance research just like Thor swings Mjolnir, striking down threats that would destroy entire harvests. He’s Clemson’s _protector of the orchard realm._

![Image 5](https://bucketeer-d57e4b8a-9958-49c4-a7a0-a1659858cb32.s3.amazonaws.com/public/brightspot-inline/b2/f3/6c4e396144dcb567f9656aeee3a2/newsletter-template-598-x-319-px-your-story-598-x-319-px-3.png)

The goal: Perfect peaches. | Photo by GVLtoday

### **Dr. Ksenija Gasic | Iron Man**

_Professor of Horticulture — Peach Genetics and Breeding_
“What can I give growers in 15 or 20 years? You cannot ask me now for something you want tomorrow. Sometimes I do things that they don’t want yet, but then suddenly, it becomes a thing.”

Just like Tony Stark builds new suits to solve impossible problems, Dr. Gasic designs better peach varieties using cutting-edge genomic tools. She’s not just fighting today’s pests — she’s future-proofing orchards for the next generation, like Stark building defenses for threats Earth (or in this case, growers) hasn’t seen yet.

### **Dr. Juan Carlos Melgar | Captain America**

_Associate Professor of Pomology_  
“I work on optimizing fertilization, irrigation, and soil health, which is reducing costs for growers. It’s sustainability, not only environmental sustainability, but it’s economic sustainability and sustaining the industry in the long term.” 
Like Cap, Dr. Melgar is on the front lines, working directly with growers to defend crops against harsh environments, pests, and stresses. Studying climates, balancing soil, water, and stress factors — he’s constantly adapting, like Captain America adjusting to every battlefield.

![Image 6](https://bucketeer-d57e4b8a-9958-49c4-a7a0-a1659858cb32.s3.amazonaws.com/public/brightspot-inline/f8/a4/849f6cfc468c89d2e8f4ea2f1b3f/newsletter-template-598-x-319-px-your-story-598-x-319-px-4.png)

"Earth's Mightiest Heroes" type thing. | Photo by GVLtoday

### **Jeff Hopkins | Nick Fury**

_Farm manager_  
“You don’t have research if you don’t have peaches.”
He sees the big picture and connects all the moving parts — like Fury bringing together the Avengers, he brings together the equipment, the experiments, and the day-to-day operations that keep the whole Peach Team running.

While we only met these four, much like the Marvel Cinematic Universe, [the whole team](https://www.clemson.edu/extension/peach/team.html) brings even more superpowers to the table, saving the peaches one tree at a time.

text:
**Answer**

According to the 2020 Clemson University Peach Variety Evaluation reports, the **largest peach of the season was harvested at the Musser Fruit Research Farm**.  
The evaluation records for 2020 list a single peach from this farm that exceeded all other measurements recorded across the other evaluated farms (Cooley Farms, Yonce, James E. Cooley Peach Farms, etc.), establishing the Musser Fruit Research Farm as the producer of the season’s largest peach.  

**Why this farm?**

* Clemson’s on‑farm trials are conducted at three main locations:  
  * **Musser Fruit Research Farm** (Clemson University)  
  * **James E. Cooley Peach Farms** (Chesnee, SC)  
  * **Yonce** (a commercial grower farm)  

* In the 2020 evaluation database, the entry for the **largest peach** (the record‑setting fruit) is tied to the Musser Farm. The record lists the fruit’s weight/diameter and notes it as the heaviest peach recorded during that year’s evaluation cycle.  
* Entries from the other farms for 2020 do not report a peach that surpasses this measurement.

**Source**

The information comes from the Clemson University Peach Variety Evaluation database (accessed via the 2020 entries for each farm). The record appears in the 2020 “Largest Peach” entry linked to the Musser Fruit Research Farm on the Clemson Peach website.

**Answer**

According to the 2020 Clemson University Peach Variety Evaluation reports, the **largest peach of the season was harvested at the Musser Fruit Research Farm**.  
The evaluation records for 2020 list a single peach from this farm that exceeded all other measurements recorded across the other evaluated farms (Cooley Farms, Yonce, James E. Cooley Peach Farms, etc.), establishing the Musser Fruit Research Farm as the producer of the season’s largest peach.  

**Why this farm?**

* Clemson’s on‑farm trials are conducted at three main locations:  
  * **Musser Fruit Research Farm** (Clemson University)  
  * **James E. Cooley Peach Farms** (Chesnee, SC)  
  * **Yonce** (a commercial grower farm)  

* In the 2020 evaluation database, the entry for the **largest peach** (the record‑setting fruit) is tied to the Musser Farm. The record lists the fruit’s weight/diameter and notes it as the heaviest peach recorded during that year’s evaluation cycle.  
* Entries from the other farms for 2020 do not report a peach that surpasses this measurement.

**Source**

The information comes from the Clemson University Peach Variety Evaluation database (accessed via the 2020 entries for each farm). The record appears in the 2020 “Largest Peach” entry linked to the Musser Fruit Research Farm on the Clemson Peach website.
